problem: Robots viewing a room through a doorway lack a belief over hidden geometry and target-object locations; existing priors are handcrafted, discrete, or coarse, and deterministic completion gives a single (possibly wrong) world that is hard to use for configuration-space planning.
motivation: Exploration is costly, so planning before entering needs a queryable prior over unseen occupancy and semantics. Pretrained generative vision models implicitly encode layout and object regularities and could be sampled zero-shot to give such priors, but no benchmark exists to test this.
key_idea: Compose a VLM gate, FLUX outpainting, SegFormer segmentation and DepthPro depth to sample many labeled 3D point-cloud worlds of the hidden room from one doorway RGB crop, and use them as an empirical belief for a sampling-based planner.
insight: Sampling many hypotheses matters: a single generated completion (1-sample) plans worse than a uniform prior (target reach 0.041 vs 0.069, collision 0.971 vs 0.815), while the 100-sample belief reaches 0.231 with 0.428 collision. The OPR-vs-K ablation shows OPR@1m rising from 0.544 at K=1 to 0.925 at K=100, with more samples helping mainly out-of-crop targets. Uniform random sampling of the same search volume gets only 3.9% best OPR, so success comes from the generative semantic prior, not volume size.
method: VLM gate: Qwen2.5-VL 7B scores target plausibility via room-posterior marginalization with a room-object table; gate gamma=0.40 skips implausible absent queries, GT-present misses fall back to a uniform bbox in the strict evaluation.
Outpainting: FLUX.1-Fill-dev (INT4 Nunchaku, cached) outpaints 500 px on the doorway side conditioned on a VLM-written target prompt, N=100 seeded samples, observed evidence preserved.
Segmentation: ADE20K SegFormer-B5 masks collapsed to 10 MatterDoor classes, threshold 0.25 confidence and 0.5% area.
Depth lifting: DepthPro metric depth with known intrinsics, RANSAC affine alignment to crop depth, floor-plane estimation, outlier removal, giving labeled 3D point clouds (~1 s/sample).

Planner: PRM roadmap in SE(2) for a Stretch robot, FCL collision checks against each sampled world, and A* over the edge weights to maximize p_plan (joint collision-free reach probability), similar to minimum-constraint-removal planning of Lu et al.

MatterDoor benchmark: 100 doorway-side contexts x 10 objects = 1000 queries from Matterport3D, 184 GT-present instances, 173 NavMesh-verified planning tasks, with metrics D_sem, p_det, mOPR/bOPR, Chamfer, energy score and GT-replay planning metrics.

setting.backbone: Qwen2.5-VL 7B + FLUX.1-Fill-dev (INT4) + SegFormer-B5 + DepthPro, all frozen and pretrained
setting.training_data: none (training-free, zero-shot composition of pretrained models)
setting.observation: single egocentric RGB doorway crop plus target object label (known camera intrinsics)
setting.action_space: planned SE(2) base trajectories for a Stretch robot via PRM roadmap (offline, simulated)
setting.simulator: Matterport3D meshes with NavMesh replay (simulated Stretch robot)
setting.privileged: none for generation or planning apart from known Matterport intrinsics and observed crop depth alignment; ground-truth geometry is used only for post-hoc evaluation (GT oracle baseline is not deployable)

numbers.eval_set_note: 184 GT-present target instances from the 1000-query benchmark; N=100 samples each
numbers.extra: 100 samples per task; VLM gate gamma=0.40 with fallback

numbers.backbone: Qwen2.5-VL 7B + FLUX.1-Fill-dev INT4 + SegFormer-B5 + DepthPro + PRM planner
numbers.extra: success threshold 1.0 m in GT replay; planning ~79 s per task

numbers_note: Custom benchmark (MatterDoor) only; no standard navigation benchmark results. Split is the whole benchmark, with no official train/val split.
results: On MatterDoor, the sampled priors realize the queried target in 90.3% of samples and reach 92.5% best OPR@1m, versus 3.9% for uniform random search-volume sampling; D_sem is 0.144 versus 0.642 for a uniform object prior. In GT-replay planning, target reach is 0.231 versus 0.069 (Uniform) and 0.041 (1-sample), and collision drops to 0.428 from 0.815.
limitations: Single source dataset (Matterport3D) with only 5 room types and 10 object classes; small evaluation (100 contexts, 173 planning tasks) and absolute planning success is still low (0.231 vs GT oracle 0.925).
Open-loop offline priors only, in simulation with no real-robot tests; sampled-belief planning is slow (~79 s per task vs ~1.6 s), and outpainting occasionally breaks room layout.
No matched direct RGB-to-3D baseline (e.g., VMem) could be scored; the baselines are weak heuristics (uniform, centroid, frontier), so the comparison is limited.
builds_on: Sampling-based planning under environment uncertainty (Lu et al. 2024)
